  An implementation-independent conformance view of the same shared

\DraftNotice

\begin{abstract}
This document converts the shared SCI-CAL v0.1 scientific authority, as
explained by Science-Team Rationale r0.4, into
observable conformance conditions. A candidate realizes a typed, occurrence-
scoped transformation from admitted \code{xs} samples to top-of-atmosphere
point-source-peak \(\mjybeam\), applies selected \code{flxscale} and target
atmosphere correction exactly once, propagates conditional uncertainty with
the identical operator, maintains a complete nuisance ledger, and emits
resolvable lineage and truthful validity/quality state. This view does not
prescribe present software structure and does not assert that any
implementation conforms. The common numbered requirements are the only
normative clauses; the procedures here describe evidence for them. Open
scientific-owner decisions remain authority gates with claim-specific
consequences. Candidate metadata or implementation behavior cannot close one.
\end{abstract}

\clearpage

\section{Conformance object and non-claims}
\label{sec:eng-purpose}

The object under review is one complete SCI-CAL transformation for a coherent
observation or declared segment, including its inputs, resolved state,
realized numerical outputs, uncertainty products, validity/quality state,
canonical lineage, and compact product links. A numeric array alone is not a
conformance object.

Conformance is evaluated against the common definitions, equations,
assumptions, requirements, and edge predictions included below. The review
does not infer scientific meaning from names, defaults, row positions, file
placement, or historical behavior. It does not map requirements to current
files, functions, classes, configuration keys, or tests. Such a mapping, if
later authorized, is a separate implementation audit.

This r0.3 engineering view is the semantic companion to Science-Team
Rationale r0.4 and its Q01--Q09 decision register. Retaining every formal ID is
necessary but not sufficient for consistency: open authority, scientific
ownership, transfer validity, broadband convention, and ordering limitations
must also survive into a conformance disposition.

A structural pass establishes only the first claim layer in
Table~\ref{tab:claim-layers}. Atmosphere representation and observational
performance require their own evidence. Its strongest structural-policy state
is \Term{science-qualification-eligible}, never an achieved
\code{science-qualified} or \code{calibrated-science} claim. The latter claims
remain governed by the separate-evidence threshold in \Req{049}. No production
state follows from this draft.

\section{Conformance evaluation sequence}
\label{sec:eng-sequence}

The sequence below is explanatory rather than an implementation architecture.
It groups the observables that the common requirements place at the cold
boundary before a hot sample calculation can have scientific meaning.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{E\arabic*.},leftmargin=*]
\item \Term{Resolve authority gates.} Load the exact Q01--Q09 snapshot and
  apply each open item's recorded consequence to the requested output or
  claim. A conditional algebra fixture may still be evaluated when explicitly
  labeled, but an open decision cannot be promoted to approved physical
  meaning.

\item \Term{Normalize the request.} Establish that the measured stream is
  \code{xs}, the target is top-of-atmosphere point-source-peak
  \(\mjybeam\), the physical input and photometric-convention states are
  declared, and the requested/effective distinction is recorded.

\item \Term{Resolve occurrence identity.} Validate acquisition keys, the
  column relation, source and selected child APT identities, local row
  occurrences, target-to-source edges, approved transformation, delivery
  identity, and array/network constraints. Establish exact cardinality for
  the selected support before evaluating factors.

\item \Term{Resolve factor causality.} Admit one selected \code{flxscale} per
  detector occurrence, resolve its producer-owned generating record, verify
  its direction and reference plane, classify the child transformation and
  pointing-correction ancestry, and reject opaque or duplicate factor roles.

\item \Term{Resolve atmosphere support.} Validate opacity and airmass meaning,
  time coverage/bracketing, segment quality, exact content-bound operator,
  node support, ordinate orientation, and passband identity/limitations. In
  the present draft, \Assump{011} necessarily stops numeric calibration here.

\item \Term{Resolve ordering and broadband compatibility.} Bind the declared
  pre-CAL affine boundary and pipeline-order state. Verify that the source
  factor, target atmosphere, and output share an approved compatible
  photometric/passband convention, or carry the exact unavailable limitation.

\item \Term{Evaluate once.} Only on support admitted by the applicable
  authority gates, evaluate
  Equations~\eqref{eq:piecewise-operator}, \eqref{eq:multiplier}, and
  \eqref{eq:signal}. Record factor-instance application counts and numeric
  factor ranges. Invalid occurrences remain outside the domain rather than
  becoming zeros.

\item \Term{Propagate conditional uncertainty.} Apply
  Equation~\eqref{eq:conditional-covariance} or
  \eqref{eq:variance-weight} to the identical support. Preserve full
  correlations when supplied; otherwise record the exact available form or an
  unavailable state.

\item \Term{Resolve nuisance and response claims.} Complete the required
  nuisance ledger, retain correlations, link the originating Beammap response
  separately from any realized downstream response, and withhold total or
  point-source-peak claims that lack their conditions.

\item \Term{Publish reconstructible state.} Emit the validity tuple, reason
  codes, one canonical lineage record, and resolvable product links. State the
  status of structural, representation, and observational claims separately.
\end{enumerate}

\label{sec:eng-owner-gates}

Table~\ref{tab:eng-owner-gates} carries the Science-Team Rationale r0.4

The consequence is applied to exactly the affected signal, interpretation, or
claim; an unrelated open item does not erase a separately valid quantity.

\label{tab:eng-owner-gates}\\

SCI-CAL-OWNER-Q01 & Physical \code{xs} definition & Complete input/factor units, sign,

an unapproved child transformation cannot calibrate. \\
SCI-CAL-OWNER-Q05 & Broadband photometric convention & Complete monochromatic mJy meaning
and cross-array spectral comparison are unavailable; the source-factor,
atmosphere, and output conventions may not be presumed compatible. \\
SCI-CAL-OWNER-Q06 & Atmosphere operator & Contract-supported numerical atmosphere
correction and calibrated numerical SCI-CAL output are unavailable under
\Assump{011}. \\
SCI-CAL-OWNER-Q07 & Opacity/segment policy rationale & The adopted limits remain binding,
but their physical rationale, segment owner, split policy, and change
authority may not be inferred. \\
SCI-CAL-OWNER-Q08 & Numerical uncertainty products & Total calibrated uncertainty and
significance remain unavailable; conditional measurement uncertainty retains
its narrower meaning. \\
SCI-CAL-OWNER-Q09 & Validated-science criteria & No achieved atmosphere-fidelity,
repeatability, absolute-recovery, science-qualified, calibrated-science, or
production-readiness claim is available. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\section{Evidence package for a future audit or clean implementation}
\label{sec:eng-evidence}

A review package can remain implementation neutral while exposing enough
evidence to falsify the contract. The recommended evidence inventory is:

\begin{itemize}
\item a content-bound Q01--Q09 owner-decision snapshot plus claim-by-claim
  fixtures demonstrating that each open state blocks exactly its recorded
  output or interpretation and cannot be closed by candidate metadata;
\item immutable input and resolved-state records for at least two observations
  with deliberately different detector subsets, selected APTs, associations,
  atmosphere states, and response bases;
\item source-calibration, TolProj association/child-transform, TolTECA
  delivery, and SCI-CAL consumption records, including identity-transform,
  approved-transform, out-of-domain-transform, and no-reinterpretation cases;
\item the exact operator and passband content identities, node inventory,
  orientation, support, and opacity interpolation records;
\item broadband-compatibility and pipeline-boundary records, including a case
  in which Q06 is resolved while Q01--Q05 remain open and unpromoted;
\item a machine-resolvable factor ledger showing role and application count,
  including one corrected-APT ancestry challenge;
\item scalar and dense-vector conditional uncertainty fixtures, plus nuisance
  covariance fixtures at detector, array, observation, cohort, and global
  scopes;
\item identity metamorphic cases covering keyed permutations, proven and
  broken ordered relations, network reorder, missing/duplicate keys, every
  association disposition, and irrelevant design-ID changes;
\item response fixtures for an unresolved source before and after a known
  response-changing kernel; and
\item output inventories, canonical lineage, compact links, validity tuples,
  reason codes, and claim-layer status for every case, including every
  truthful no-output state.
\end{itemize}

For each case, the evidence states expected equations and edge IDs before
execution, numeric precision and tolerances, exact identity expectations, and
whether a mismatch invalidates a detector, segment, or entire required output.
A skipped required case remains unavailable. Structural fixtures do not stand
in for the separately proposed atmosphere representation and observational
studies in Section~\ref{sec:validation-evidence}.

\section{Conformance disposition}
\label{sec:eng-disposition}

A future reviewer can use four non-overlapping dispositions:

\begin{longtable}{L{0.22\linewidth}L{0.66\linewidth}}
\caption{Disposition meanings.}\label{tab:eng-disposition}\\
\toprule
Disposition & Meaning \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Disposition & Meaning \\
\midrule
\endhead
Structurally conformant & All applicable numbered requirements and
predeclared structural predictions pass on the exact reviewed candidate and
support; this says nothing stronger about atmosphere fidelity or performance. \\
Nonconformant & One or more applicable equations, requirements, identity or
support invariants, uncertainty transforms, lineage conditions, or truthful
state outputs fail. \\
Unavailable & Required authority or evidence is absent. This is the current
claim-specific disposition for every open Q01--Q09 consequence, including the
numeric-atmosphere disposition under \Assump{011}; it is not a pass or a
failure of an untested implementation. \\
Not applicable & A requirement's premise is demonstrably absent and the
canonical record gives the scientific justification, for example a pointing-
correction premise shown to be absent and marked \code{not_applicable}. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

Atmosphere representation fidelity and observational performance receive
separate dispositions and evidence. Their provisional numerical targets never
convert ``unavailable'' into ``pass''.

\section{Engineering conclusion}
\label{sec:eng-conclusion}

The engineering conformance surface is finite and falsifiable: typed input,
layered identity, unique association, producer-owned source calibration,
approved child transformation, immutable delivery, selected-child factor
authority, once-only composition, supported atmosphere evaluation, broadband
and order status, identical uncertainty transfer, truthful quality/validity,
response-basis preservation, and package-level reconstructibility. No current
implementation mapping is part of this view.

Until the owner binds the missing operator record, the correct conformance
behavior for any requested numeric atmosphere calibration is an explicit
unavailable/no-calibrated-output state. Choosing nodes, orientation, support,
or a fallback inside an implementation would be an unauthorized scientific
decision. Binding that record resolves Q06 only. It cannot close Q01--Q05 or
Q07--Q09, supply missing producer or transformation authority, establish
broadband compatibility or transfer validity, or enable an end-to-end
response claim. A structural disposition is available only for the exact
claims whose required owner gates are closed and remains no stronger than
\code{science-qualification-eligible}; it does not by itself establish an
achieved \code{science-qualified} or \code{calibrated-science} claim.
